item.title: US financial crimes bureau discloses ‘cybersecurity incident’
item.description:
The Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed on Tuesday that it's investigating a "cybersecurity incident." The bureau, which is part of the Treasury Department, said it's looking into an "incident that resulted in unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems." It hasn't offered any information about the full scope or source of the breach, but FinCEN has taken some systems offline as a precaution.

item.title: Why the US Army is about to blow up nearly 10,000 pounds of unstable explosives in Iowa
item.description:
The US Army is moving ahead with plans to detonate the nation's stockpile of lead azide at an ammunition plant in Middletown, Iowa, at approximately 9:00AM CST on Wednesday. The Verge reached out to experts on what to expect, and will keep this post updated.

What material is the Army planning to detonate?

There are 68 drums holding about 9,700 pounds of lead azide, an unstable chemical compound created to detonate munitions like grenades. item.title: Huawei found guilty of stealing trade secrets
item.description:
A jury has found Huawei guilty of stealing US trade secrets, as reported earlier by NBC News and Bloomberg. The verdict, handed down in a federal court in New York, concludes a years-long legal battle that accused the Chinese telecom giant of stealing source code and proprietary technology from several companies, including T-Mobile, Cisco, and Motorola.

item.title: GTA VI PC recompilation project shut down by Take-Two
item.description:
Game modding communities are racing to get Grand Theft Auto VI running on PC, but one big effort has been taken down by Take-Two today. Leonida, a fan project by 15-year-old "NotRexed," has vanished after a DMCA takedown notice from GTA VI publisher Take-Two.

Leonida was designed to translate a leaked GTA VI Xbox build to run natively on Windows. Cyberleek, the leaker who posted multiple GTA VI gameplay videos over the summer, published a full Xbox build of the game earlier this week. The leak has kicked recompilation efforts up a notch, as modders race to reverse-engineer the game's code and rebuild it into native PC code.

item.title: Jensen Huang reportedly tells Nvidia staff it’s ‘not true’ Trump got him rehired
item.description:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to staff during his first all-hands since returning to the company, while attempting to distance himself from the narrative that the White House and tech leaders helped him get his job back, according to reports from Bloomberg, The New York Times, and The Handbasket's Marisa Kabas.

During the meeting, Huang reportedly called claims that President Donald Trump was directly involved in his reinstatement - an idea publicly promoted by Trump himself - "completely untrue." item.title: The clock is running out for America’s most contentious spying law
item.description:
Weeks before the end of the legislative session, some members of Congress are scrambling to reauthorize a controversial warrantless wiretapping authority, possibly by attaching it to a must-pass military spending bill. Sen. Mike Rounds (R-SD) told Politico that Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA) could be attached to the National Defense Authorization Act. It's the latest in a grueling fight over a major spying rule that hasn't technically lapsed.

item.title: Amazon is knocking almost $50 off six months of Apple TV
item.description:
Streaming deals aren’t as plentiful as they used to be, but they’re still around if you know where to look. One that caught our eye is an offer for Apple TV for those with an Amazon account in the US. Apple’s streaming service usually costs $14.99 per month, but following this page will let you get it for $6.99 for your first six months (totaling $42 versus $90 without the deal). Amazon hasn’t shared how long this offer will be available for, so I’d strike on it sooner than later.

Apple TV subscription

Where to Buy:

  • $15 $7 at Amazon (monthly for 6 months)

The subscription includes exclusive access to Formula 1 races and Major League Soccer matches, not to mention a bunch of acclaimed shows like Severance, Silo, The Morning Show, Pachinko, Pluribus, Slow Horses, and many more. (Yo Gabba GabbaLand is amazing for kids who enjoy music.) The service also somewhat recently added movies made outside of Apple’s studios, including classics like Arrival, Dead Poets Society, and Anchorman, to name a few. While the service is technically free of ads, Apple advertises plenty of its own original programming as skippable preroll ahead of content.
